name: VoxCPM
tagline: OpenBMB tokenizer-free TTS (MiniCPM backbone + diffusion head). VoxCPM2 clones from reference audio alone or continues from a transcribed prompt.

reference.recommended: One clean clip of 5 to 20 s. Add the exact transcript for the closest clone

suggested.label: VoxCPM2 (2B)
suggested.note: Reference-only and continuation cloning. About 5 GB, about 8 GB VRAM.

options.label: Auto
options.help: Reference + continuation when a transcript is given, otherwise reference only.

options.label: Reference only
options.help: Copies the timbre from the clip without needing a transcript. Delivery follows the text and the style instruction, not the reference.

options.label: Continuation
options.help: The model treats the reference as the beginning of the same recording and continues it. Copies rhythm and emotion too. Needs an exact transcript.

options.label: Reference + continuation
options.help: Uses both paths. Closest overall similarity (the 'ultimate cloning' setup). Needs an exact transcript.

help.summary: How the reference is used. VoxCPM2 has an isolated reference path and a continuation path.
help.increase: Continuation and combined copy prosody, emotion and room sound in addition to timbre.
help.decrease: Reference only copies the timbre and lets you control the delivery with a style instruction.
help.tip: Use combined for a faithful clone and reference only when you want to change the emotion.

help.summary: Free-form instruction for speed, emotion or style, added in parentheses in front of the text. Only applied in 'Reference only' mode.
help.increase: A concrete instruction such as 'whispering, slow' changes the delivery while keeping the cloned timbre.
help.decrease: Leave empty for a neutral reading.
help.tip: English or Chinese instructions are the most reliable.

help.summary: How many takes to generate one after another. With Seed -1 every take gets its own random seed. With a fixed seed, take n uses seed + n - 1.
help.tip: 2 or 3 takes make it easy to pick the best reading.

help.summary: Random seed for the language model and the diffusion noise. -1 picks a new random seed for every take.
help.increase: A fixed value reproduces the same take with the same inputs and settings.
help.decrease: -1 gives a fresh variation every run.
help.tip: Copy the seed of a good take from the result card.

help.summary: Classifier-free guidance of the diffusion head. Controls how strictly the audio follows the text and the voice prompt.
help.increase: Clearer articulation and closer adherence. Too high sounds harsh, over-pronounced or metallic.
help.decrease: Softer and more relaxed, but less precise and occasionally mumbled.

help.summary: Number of diffusion steps used to generate each audio patch.
help.increase: More detailed, cleaner audio. Time grows roughly linearly.
help.tip: 10 is the default. 15 to 25 for final renders, 6 for drafts.

help.summary: Removes long silences from the reference with voice activity detection before encoding.
help.increase: On helps when the reference has long gaps, which otherwise turn into long pauses in the output.
help.decrease: Off keeps the reference exactly as recorded.
help.tip: Turn on if outputs start with or contain unnatural pauses.

help.summary: Runs the ZipEnhancer noise suppressor on the reference before cloning. The first use downloads the model from ModelScope.
help.increase: On removes background noise and hum that would otherwise be cloned too.
help.decrease: Off keeps the original character of the recording, which matters for continuation mode.
help.tip: Use only for noisy references. Denoised clips are cached.

help.summary: Expands numbers, dates and symbols into words before synthesis using VoxCPM's normalizer.
help.increase: On helps Chinese and English text with numbers.
help.tip: Turn on when English text contains numbers, dates or units. The normalizer targets Chinese and English.

help.summary: Automatically regenerates when the audio is abnormally long for the text, which usually means looping or babbling.
help.increase: On makes failures much rarer at the cost of occasional extra time.
help.decrease: Off returns the first result even if it is broken.

help.summary: How many attempts are made when a bad take is detected.
help.increase: Higher success rate, longer worst-case time.

help.summary: Maximum audio length per text token before a take counts as bad. It also caps the generation length.
help.increase: Allows slower speech and long pauses before retrying.
help.decrease: Retries sooner. Too low cuts off slow, legitimate speech.
help.tip: Raise to 8 if slow readings get cut.

help.summary: Hard limit of generated audio patches.
help.tip: The bad take length ratio usually limits length first.

help.summary: Minimum number of audio patches before the model may stop.
help.increase: Prevents empty or truncated output for very short text.
